articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations on November 13, 2026, targeting individuals and entities involved in counter narcotics and counter terrorism activities.
These actions aim to disrupt financial networks supporting illicit drug trafficking and terrorist organizations globally, reinforcing the U.S. commitment to combating these threats.
Further details regarding the specific individuals and entities designated, and the implications of these actions, are available on the Treasury's website.

articles.headline: OFAC Updates Iran Designations, Targets Shadow Fleet and Aviation Networks
body: OFAC announced an update to its Iran designations on November 9, 2026, as part of 'Operation Economic Outcast,' targeting 13 individuals and companies.
These entities are accused of providing fraudulent vessel flags and maritime certifications to Iran's 'shadow fleet,' which is used to evade sanctions.
Additionally, a Türkiye-based company supporting sanctioned Iranian airlines was targeted, and an alert was issued regarding sanctions risks associated with falsely flagged vessels.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / ABA Banking Journal

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Eight Canadian Money Services Businesses for Iran Sanctions Evasion
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) designated eight Canada-based money services businesses on November 6, 2026, under Executive Order 13902.

These businesses are accused of operating in the digital asset sector of the Iranian economy, facilitating the exchange of Iranian rials and other currencies for digital assets to enable international transactions involving Iran.
This action is part of 'Operation Economic Outcast' and aims to disrupt financial networks that enable the Iranian regime and other illicit actors to move assets into and out of Iran.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / U.S. Department of the Treasury

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Cyber-related and Transnational Criminal Organizations Designations; Cuba Designations; Publishes Cuba-related Determination
body: On November 5, 2026, OFAC issued new designations targeting cyber-related activities and transnational criminal organizations, alongside new Cuba-related sanctions.

The Cuba designations included eight entities and two individuals, and identified five vessels as blocked property, targeting the Cuban regime's oil shipping networks, state-owned entities, and China-based suppliers of Cuba's military forces.
Concurrently, OFAC published a determination under Executive Order 14404, authorizing sanctions against foreign persons operating in Cuba's electronics, manufacturing, marine, and technology sectors.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / U.S. Department of State

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-related Designations, Updates Listings, Publishes Alert; Amends Venezuela-related General License
body: On November 4, 2026, OFAC announced new Iran-related designations, targeting four individuals and nine entities linked to an India-based network supporting Iran's shadow fleet.
The network, led by Suniel Kumar Sharma and Jaspreet Preeti Shahid, allegedly provided false flags and certifications to sanctioned vessels transporting Iranian petroleum.

In a separate action, OFAC issued Venezuela-related General License 5AA, replacing General License 5Z, which authorizes certain transactions involving the PDVSA 2020 8.5% bond on or after December 18, 2026.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / ABA Banking Journal

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran-related General License
body: On October 29, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued an amended Iran-related General License.
This amendment modifies existing authorizations for certain transactions involving Iran, and parties engaged in Iran-related activities should review the updated guidance carefully.
The specific details of the amendments are available on the Treasury Department's website, providing clarity on permissible activities under the updated license.

articles.region: North Korea, Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Imposes North Korea and Democratic Republic of the Congo-related Designations
body: On October 28, 2026, OFAC announced new designations targeting individuals and entities related to North Korea and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
These actions aim to counter illicit activities supporting the North Korean regime and address human rights abuses and instability in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
The designations underscore the U.S. commitment to promoting stability and human rights globally, and further details are available on the Treasury's website.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs Regarding Blocking and Rejecting Transactions and Filing Reports
body: On October 26, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued amended Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) regarding blocking and rejecting transactions and filing reports with OFAC.
These updates provide additional guidance and clarification for financial institutions and other entities on their compliance obligations under OFAC regulations.
The revised FAQs are intended to assist in navigating complex sanctions requirements and ensuring accurate reporting to the Treasury Department.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-related Designations; Belarus and North Korea Designations Removals; Issues Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses and Amended FAQs
body: On October 21, 2026, OFAC announced new Iran-related designations, alongside the removal of certain designations related to Belarus and North Korea.
The agency also issued new general licenses pertaining to Iran and Russia, and amended existing Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) to provide further guidance.
These actions reflect ongoing adjustments to U.S. sanctions policy, addressing evolving geopolitical landscapes and humanitarian considerations.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.
